title: Union Minister Shri Rajiv Ranjan Singh Highlights Massive Growth in India's Livestock Sector
subtitle:
Over 50 Lakh Farmers Credit-Linked Under KCC; 6.4 Lakh Participate in Digital Training
Accelerating Scientific Breeding and Fodder Development Nationally
Strengthening Doorstep Veterinary Healthcare and Disease Control
body_text:
Union Minister for Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying, Shri Rajiv Ranjan Singh alias Lalan Singh, announced major developments in India's livestock sector, detailing expanding institutional credit, digital outreach, and livestock productivity.
Credit accessibility for animal husbandry farmers reached a key milestone, with Kisan Credit Card (KCC) coverage scaling to 50.42 lakh beneficiaries in FY 2025–26, up from 15.08 lakh in 2021–22. India's annual milk production reached 247.87 million tonnes in 2024–25, comfortably surpassing domestic demand (243 million tonnes). Total dairy exports reached $407.18 million in FY 2025–26.
To boost long-term yield and genetic resilience, the Ministry is actively expanding flagship schemes across States:
Rashtriya Gokul Mission (RGM): To supplement the efforts of the States and UTs in promoting scientific breeding, Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying, Government of India(GoI) is implementing Rashtriya Gokul Mission (RGM) since December 2014 for development and conservation of indigenous breeds, genetic upgradation of bovine population and enhancement of milk production and productivity thereby making milk production more remunerative to farmers.
National Livestock Mission (NLM): In order to promote scientific breeding and improve fodder quality in the country, the Department of Animal Husbandry & Dairying, Government of India is implementing the scheme of National Livestock Mission since the financial year 2014-15. The scheme of National Livestock Mission (NLM) aims towards employment generation, entrepreneurship development, increase in per animal productivity and thus targeting increased production of meat, goat milk, egg and wool under the umbrella scheme Development Programme. The concept of NLM Scheme is to develop the entrepreneur in order to create the forward and backward linkage for the produce available at the unorganized sector and to link with the organized sector.
The major initiatives undertaken by, Government of India (GOI) under the National Livestock Mission (NLM) and Livestock Health and Disease Control Programme (LHDCP) to promote livestock development and strengthen animal healthcare services in Tamil Nadu during the last five years are as below:-
50% capital subsidyprovided under NLM-EDP to individuals, Farmer Producer Organisations (FPOs), Self-Help Groups (SHGs), Joint Liability Groups (JLGs), Farmer Cooperative Organisations (FCOs), and Section 8 companies. The NLM scheme focuses on Breed Development of Livestock & Poultry, Feed and Fodder development, Research & Development, Livestock Insurance and Extension. 100% financial assistance is provided under LHDCP to all the States/UTs for prevention of economically important livestock diseases namely Foot and Mouth Disease (FMD), Brucellosis, Peste des Petits Ruminants (PPR) and Classical Swine Fever (CSF) through vaccination. Further, financial assistance is provided to States/ UTs on sharing basis for State prioritised activities such asvaccination against other livestock diseases, control of emergent and exotic diseases, strengthening of laboratory, disease surveillance, training and awareness. Financial assistance is provided to the State of Tamil Nadu on sharing basis for operation of 245 Mobile Veterinary Units (MVU)to deliver veterinary services at farmer’s doorstep.

enrichment.summary: Union Minister Rajiv Ranjan Singh (Lalan Singh) highlighted growth in India's livestock sector, noting Kisan Credit Card (KCC) coverage for animal husbandry farmers rose to 50.42 lakh beneficiaries in FY 2025-26 from 15.08 lakh in 2021-22. India's milk production reached 247.87 million tonnes in 2024-25, exceeding domestic demand of 243 million tonnes, while dairy exports touched $407.18 million in FY 2025-26. The Ministry also detailed flagship schemes—Rashtriya Gokul Mission, National Livestock Mission, and Livestock Health and Disease Control Programme—including specific achievements in Tamil Nadu such as 245 Mobile Veterinary Units and disease control support.
enrichment.context:
The livestock sector is a critical pillar of India's rural economy, contributing significantly to farmer incomes, especially for smallholders and landless households who rely on dairy and animal rearing as supplementary income. The Kisan Credit Card scheme, originally designed for crop loans, was extended to animal husbandry and fisheries farmers in 2018-19 to provide affordable institutional credit and reduce dependence on informal moneylenders; the sharp rise in KCC coverage reflects intensified government outreach and financial inclusion efforts. India has been the world's largest milk producer for decades, a legacy of the White Revolution (Operation Flood) launched in the 1970s, and continued growth in production alongside rising exports signals both productivity gains and expanding global market access for Indian dairy products.

The Rashtriya Gokul Mission (since 2014) focuses on conserving indigenous cattle breeds and improving genetic quality through breeding technologies like IVF and sexed semen, aiming to enhance milk yield while preserving native breed diversity. The National Livestock Mission (since 2014-15) supports entrepreneurship in poultry, meat, wool, and fodder sectors, addressing gaps in the unorganized livestock economy. The Livestock Health and Disease Control Programme ensures nationwide vaccination against economically significant diseases like Foot and Mouth Disease and Peste des Petits Ruminants, critical for protecting livestock assets, sustaining exports (many countries require disease-free certification), and preventing zoonotic spillover risks. Doorstep veterinary services via Mobile Veterinary Units represent an effort to improve last-mile healthcare access in rural and remote areas.

prelims_questions.question: The Rashtriya Gokul Mission, aimed at conservation and genetic upgradation of indigenous bovine breeds, has been implemented since which year?
prelims_questions.explanation: The release states the Rashtriya Gokul Mission has been implemented by the Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying since December 2014.

prelims_questions.question: Which of the following diseases is NOT covered under the Livestock Health and Disease Control Programme (LHDCP) for 100% financial assistance to States/UTs for vaccination, as per the release?
prelims_questions.explanation: The release specifies 100% financial assistance under LHDCP for vaccination against FMD, Brucellosis, PPR, and Classical Swine Fever (CSF); Avian Influenza is not listed among these four diseases.
